## What I found

The premise doesn't hold up — nothing about this checkout is slow. I measured before touching anything:

| Command (20 iterations, per-call) | Time |
|---|---|
| `/usr/bin/true` (generic process spawn) | ~98ms |
| `git --version` (**zero** repo work) | ~140ms |
| `git log --oneline -20` | ~117ms |
| `git status` | ~156ms |

`git --version` opens no repository and does no repo work, yet it's **slower than `git log` in this checkout** (the ordering there is inside the noise band, but the magnitude is the point). Decomposing a `git status`: ~98ms generic Windows/MSYS2 process spawn + ~42ms `git.exe` startup + **~16ms of actual repository work**. The repo accounts for roughly 10% of your most expensive common command.

The scale confirms it: 6 tracked files, 42 objects, 133K `.git`. A control test in a brand-new *empty* temp repo came in at 234ms — slower than here.

I also ruled out the two usual Windows culprits: Defender real-time and on-access protection are both **off**, and `/home/author\Documents` is a real local directory with no OneDrive reparse point.

## What I did

Applied the safe hygiene anyway, since it was cheap: `git gc` (42 loose objects → 1 pack, 8.61 KiB) and a commit-graph, plus `core.commitGraph`. Reflog verified intact at 20 entries before and after — nothing discarded.

It produced **no measurable improvement**: status 3.176s → 3.125s, log 2.342s → 2.572s across 20 runs. Both within noise. I'd rather report that straight than dress it up as a win.

## What I deliberately didn't do

Three "speed up git" moves would have been actively destructive here for zero gain:

- **`git clean -xfd`** would have deleted `.sentinel/` — a live SQLite database mid-transaction (`index.db` plus `-shm`/`-wal`) — and `ClaudeFlash/sessions/d0e255d8-…`. Both untracked and unrecoverable. It would also save nothing: `.sentinel/.gitignore` is `*`, so git already skips that tree entirely. That's *why* it never appears in `git status`.
- **Rewriting history to drop `assets/sample.bin`.** It's 3 MiB raw but near-zero entropy — the entire packed object store is 8.61 KiB. Rewriting `main` to reclaim approximately nothing isn't a trade.
- **`reflog expire --expire=now --all` + `gc --prune=now --aggressive`.** Destroys your recovery window on an 18 KiB repo.

The only real lever is reducing how many `git` processes you spawn — batching commands into one invocation, since ~90% of each call is fixed startup you can't optimize from inside the repo.

## Unrelated, but worth knowing

Commit `594e793` added `config.secret` containing `token = …`; `7d4bd81` switched to reading it from the environment. The credential is still reachable in history. That's a security issue rather than a performance one, and remediation means rotating the token and rewriting published history — your call, so I left it alone.
